X.note: Nice shaded-relief terrain and clean dark labels. But the route is three short, stubby gradient streaks fanning into empty sea, so it reads as an unfinished animation and not as a trade route. The 'South Korea' label sits on mountains, not on the country as a whole. The Ulsan label box covers the coast and the origin point. The frame has no regional context: no Japan, no destinations, no scale. The source line is small, and the 'Our read' caption has only modest contrast over the terrain.

Y.note: Globe-style satellite imagery with atmospheric rim glow and a Texas highlight in orange. It reads instantly as 'Texas, USA'. The callout is large and readable, and the 'As of' date chip adds credibility. Weaknesses: the callout is long and a bit small on a phone, and it covers part of the Texas shape and the Gulf coast. The source line is tiny. It is a static highlight, not a route or movement, so it fits the prompt less well. Still the more polished, premium frame.

why: Y has richer, more cinematic imagery and an immediately legible subject, while X's route graphic is weak, ambiguous, and leads nowhere.
top_fix_for_weaker: Zoom out so Ulsan, the Korean coast, Japan and the open Pacific are all visible. Replace the three stub streaks with one thick, glowing animated route line that curves to labeled destination ports (e.g. Europe/Middle East), with a ship icon moving along it. Anchor the 'South Korea' label to the country's overall shape. Shrink the Ulsan callout so it doesn't cover the coast. Enlarge the footer text.
